subject: chemistry
title: Organic Chemistry Adventure 3: Mechanisms — SN1 vs SN2
welcome_lead: Today you'll compare SN1 and SN2 reactions — the heart of organic mechanisms.
meta_desc: Chemistry HL — nucleophilic substitution SN1 vs SN2, kinetics, stereochemistry.
final_note: You learned SN1 is two-step (carbocation intermediate), SN2 is one-step (backside attack); SN1 favours 3° + polar protic, SN2 favours 1° + polar aprotic.

walkthroughs.body_html:
One step, concerted: nucleophile attacks back of C as leaving group leaves.

Rate = k[R-X][Nu⁻] (second order).

Stereochemistry: inversion (Walden inversion).

Favoured by: primary halogenoalkanes, strong nucleophile, polar aprotic solvent.

Two steps:
1. Slow: R-X → R⁺ + X⁻ (carbocation forms).
2. Fast: R⁺ + Nu⁻ → R-Nu.

Rate = k[R-X] only (first order).

Stereochemistry: racemic mixture (carbocation planar; attack either side).

Favoured by: tertiary (stable carbocation), polar protic solvent.

Primary halogenoalkanes → almost always SN2.
Tertiary → almost always SN1.
Secondary → either depending on conditions.

Leaving group ability: I > Br > Cl > F (weaker C-X bond).

Solvent polarity: SN1 boosted by polar protic; SN2 boosted by polar aprotic.

Free radical halogenation of alkanes: initiation (UV), propagation (Cl· + RH), termination.
